annotation.title_clean: Protomoral Machines: The Evolution of Morality as a Guideline for Robot Ethics
annotation.title_en: Protomoral Machines: The Evolution of Morality as a Guideline for Robot Ethics
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 335: Culturally Sustainable Social Robotics (Robophilosophy 2020), IOS Press
annotation.summary_en: Robophilosophy 2020 conference paper on moral agency in robots. Takes an evolutionary perspective and argues for a middle-range approach: neither current ethical concerns nor far-future questions of genuine machine morality, but designing 'protomoral' machines informed by the evolution of human morality. Only the abstract is available.
key_provisions_or_claims: Two questions: how to make robots behave ethically, and whether genuinely moral machines are possible.
Argues for a middle-range perspective between present-day ethical concerns and far-future theoretical issues.
Proposes reflecting on what creating protomoral machines would mean.
Claims the evolution of human morality can guide robot ethics.
